name: Firestorm
description: A field of volumetric flame columns flown through at ground level. Near columns overrun the top of the frame, far ones fall away to a lit smoke horizon, and embers rise between them.

speed.description: How fast the flames lick upward.

walk.description: How fast the camera moves into the field. 0 stands still in it.

turbulence.description: Noise frequency eating into the columns. Low is smooth teardrops, high is torn and ragged.

column.description: Base radius of a flame column, against a spacing of 2.1. Past about 1.0 the columns touch and the field stops being columns at all — the camera is then permanently inside fuel and the frame comes out as one flat wall of smoke.

density.description: Opacity per unit of fuel. High makes a solid body, low makes a haze you can see through.

steps.description: March samples. Below ~32 the volume starts to band.

tint.description: Blend toward the project palette. 0 keeps the native orange-to-blue gradient. Past about 0.6 a cool palette stops reading as fire at all.
